title: Take Your Time, Dad
style: Alternative R&B with restrained post-punk arrangement; close-miked, dry production; dry drum kit, wiry melodic bass, clipped clean guitar; steady midtempo pulse; low conversational female mezzo, opening melody on “I can stay,” a full-beat pause before “I can wait,” stacked hook harmonies and layered octave doubles, final chorus voice brought forward, bass and drums dropped before the last lines.
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Maureen held the phone up to your bed
three days after the stroke.
You were awake by then.
I didn’t even know you had diabetes.

Thanksgiving twenty-two,
last time I’d been home to Worcester.
Too busy in twenty-three.
Then the inquiry.
I left the practice, handed in my license,
moved to Bogotá.
Once or twice a month,
one of us would text.

[Verse 2]
I cleared my appointments,
took the next flight into Logan.
I sent Thomas and María Teresa
what I had on the calendar at Índigo.
Thomas wrote, “Take your time.”
I read it twice at the gate.

You were more yourself in Worcester
than you’d been on the phone.
One side barely moved.
“Too early to tell,” they said.
I used to say that, too.
I knew how much it left open.

[Chorus]
Take your time, Dad.
I can stay.
Tell me what you want me to hold.
I can wait.

[Verse 3]
Maureen and I brought you home the next week.
She had to get back to work.
I could stay.
I’d find out what I had left at Índigo.
I’d find out how long the money would last.

Steven Swansen.
Dad, in my head you’re still a bull.
Now it’s bed to chair,
chair to bed.
You brace the jam jar against your chest.
I reach for it.
You’ve nearly got it.

[Final Chorus]
Take your time, Dad.
I can stay.
The lid gives a little.
I put my hands back in my lap.

[Outro]
You’re all there, Dad.
I keep saying that like it’s good news.
It is for us.
I don’t know what it is for you.
